How many times the simulator may stretch the range when frames are to spare. Squared in the full renderer: ×3 means up to ×9.
Fewer frames: a cooler, quieter computer. With V-Sync a limit above the refresh rate does nothing.
Shortens the long shadows cast by a low sun. Higher values cut them sooner.
Synchronizes frame rate with the monitor refresh rate.
Renders reflections into a cube map, so surfaces mirror the surroundings from every direction.
Alternative depth-buffer read path with MSAA; enable it if your GPU has compatibility issues.
How often reflections refresh. Less often means more frames.
How far shadows reach; the further, the softer. After the arrow: the real reach.
Sets which objects cast shadows based on material priority. Lower value = fewer shadows, higher performance.

The model DLSS rebuilds the image with. The DLSS mode follows the buffer scale: about 67% Quality, 50% Performance, 33% Ultra Performance.
Extra frames between the drawn ones. With DLSS or DLAA only. x3 and x4 need an RTX 50 card.
Less delay between the controls and the image.
Fills in reflections where SSR finds nothing. The card needs ray query.
A card's number from the list in the log, or part of its name, like RTX. Empty: chosen automatically.
Reflections of what is on screen, on wet and smooth surfaces.
Darkens corners and places where surfaces meet. GTAO is more accurate than SSAO.
GTAO only. Darkens ambient light and reflections, sun and lamps stay bright. Off: multiplies the finished image, cheaper.
Vehicle lights and street lamps with no limit on their number. Needed for scenery lamps and the cab lamp.
Shadows cast by the cab lamp, street lamps and vehicle headlights.
Small shadows where objects touch, which the shadow map misses.
Shadow cascades fitted to the scene (SDSM)
Spreads the sun shadow resolution over what is actually in view.
Light bounced off the cab walls and reflections of the interior in the windows.
Refresh the probe every N frames
The windows show the cab interior instead of the sky where SSR finds nothing.
How much of the lamp's light reflected off the walls lights the cab again. Works with the cab probe.
Number of raindrops and snowflakes in the heaviest precipitation.
Image brightness adapts to the scene, for instance entering a tunnel.
MSAA smooths the edges of objects, TAA the whole image at the cost of a slight blur. DLSS and DLAA need Vulkan and an NVIDIA RTX card, otherwise the simulator uses TAA.
Fog with sun shafts, cloud shadows and the light of lamps. Off: the simpler analytic fog.
The quality of the clouds drawn in the sky.
DLSS, frame generation, Reflex and ray tracing need Vulkan.
Needs an exe with Vulkan and a card that supports it. Otherwise the simulator starts Full or Old.
K for DLAA, Quality and Balanced, M for Performance, L for Ultra Performance. The driver may change this with an update.
The transformer model with the best image quality, but the most expensive to compute. The default for DLAA, Quality and Balanced.
Similar to K: slightly less ghosting behind moving objects at the cost of more flicker. NVIDIA recommends K instead.
The model tuned for Performance mode (about 50% scale), its default there. Works out the image exposure itself.
The model tuned for Ultra Performance mode (about 33% scale), its default there. Works out the image exposure itself.
{0} is not next to the simulator: without it the simulator cannot use this DLSS feature.
DLSS is not available on macOS.
Frame generation works with DLSS or DLAA only.
Frame generation turns Reflex on by itself, whatever is chosen here.
Needs the depth of the whole scene before its colour; without SSR and contact shadows that is an extra pass (CPU cost on OpenGL).
With the post-processing skipped the AO does not work.
Without the clustered lighting and the cab lamp as a light (gfx.lights.cab) the probe gives the reflections only.
TAA and DLSS run in the post-processing: with it skipped the edges will not be smoothed.
